title: Final: tasks without await
sub: ContinueWith, schedulers and the pool, Parallel, timers, threads and cancellation
cards/0/q: A WPF button handler, not inside any task. Where does Heavy() run?
cards/0/options/0: On the pool: outside a task TaskScheduler.Current is Default
cards/0/options/1: On the UI thread: StartNew takes the current SynchronizationContext
cards/0/options/2: On the UI thread: StartNew without a scheduler takes Current
cards/0/options/3: On a new dedicated thread: that is how StartNew works by default
cards/0/explain: Current is the scheduler of the running task, not the thread's context. A button handler is not a task, so Current is Default. The trap fires only when the code is already inside a task on a UI scheduler. It is safer not to guess and to write Task.Run.
cards/1/q: Which line throws TaskCanceledException whatever the outcome of LoadAsync?
cards/1/explain: Of the two continuations one is always skipped and moves to Canceled: on success it is log, on failure it is show. WhenAll with a cancelled task is cancelled too, and await throws TaskCanceledException.
cards/2/q: How does Task.Run(work) differ from Task.Factory.StartNew(work)? Select all.
cards/2/options/2: Task.Run unwraps the Task<Task> from an async lambda
cards/2/options/3: Task.Run allocates a dedicated thread for long work
cards/2/options/4: Task.Run picks up the caller's cancellation token by itself
cards/2/explain: Task.Run = StartNew with DenyChildAttach, TaskScheduler.Default and Unwrap for async lambdas. Only LongRunning gives a dedicated thread, and Task.Run uses only a token passed to it explicitly.
cards/3/q: Inside Task.Run a library creates a task with AttachedToParent and throws from it. What does await on your task see?
cards/3/options/0: Nothing: the child did not attach, its error stays in its own task
cards/3/options/1: An AggregateException with the child's error
cards/3/options/2: Your task waits for the child and completes together with it
cards/3/explain: DenyChildAttach on the Task.Run task silently turns the child into an independent task. No waiting, no foreign exceptions. The child's error is the concern of whoever created it.
cards/4/q: You need a report in the source row order, but the heavy formula should run on all cores. What do you add?
cards/4/explain: AsOrdered makes PLINQ return results in the source order while computing them in parallel. WithDegreeOfParallelism(1) kills the parallelism, and OrderBy sorts by value, not by position.
cards/5/q: Each thread writes only to its own hits cell, there is no race, and the check is cheap. Yet on 8 cores the loop is hardly faster than on one. Why?
cards/5/options/0: The cells share a cache line, and it bounces between cores on every write
cards/5/options/1: hits[t]++ is not atomic, and threads wait for each other on it
cards/5/options/2: Parallel.For runs iterations one by one when there are no more of them than cores
cards/5/options/3: Parallel.For takes only 2 threads by default
cards/5/explain: Eight longs are 64 bytes, one or two cache lines. To write, a core takes the line into exclusive ownership, and the copies in the other cores become invalid. That is false sharing. The cure is a local counter in the body and a single write to hits[t] at the end.
cards/5/wrong/1: Non-atomicity is dangerous when several threads write to the same cell. Here each has its own — there is nothing to lose.
cards/6/q: UploadAsync throws HttpRequestException on the fifth url. What happens?
cards/6/options/0: ct is cancelled, no new urls are taken, uploads already started finish, and await throws HttpRequestException
cards/6/options/1: The remaining urls are processed, and at the end await throws an AggregateException with all the errors
cards/6/options/2: The process crashes: the body's exception went to a pool thread, as with async void
cards/6/options/3: All started uploads are cut off on the spot, and await returns without an error
cards/6/explain: The ForEachAsync body returns a ValueTask, so the exception lands in a task, not in the pool. The first error cancels the shared ct token: the worker tasks stop taking elements, and bodies already started finish (or exit via ct). The ForEachAsync task completes with an error, and await throws the body's exception.
cards/6/wrong/2: That is what an async lambda in Parallel.ForEach would do. The ForEachAsync body is a function with a task, not async void.
cards/7/q: A PeriodicTimer has a 5 s period, and the work in the loop takes 8 s. How do the runs go?
cards/7/options/0: Back to back: one missed tick is pending, extra ones do not pile up
cards/7/options/1: Overlapping: a new instance starts every 5 s
cards/7/options/2: Every 10 s: a missed tick postpones the next one
cards/7/options/3: Missed ticks accumulate, and the loop catches up on them
cards/7/explain: While the work runs, the timer remembers at most one tick. The next wait completes immediately, and the work takes 8 s again. No overlap: a new iteration does not start until you return to WaitForNextTickAsync.
cards/8/q: A background thread (IsBackground = true) is writing a file in try/finally when Main ends. What about finally?
cards/8/options/0: It does not run: the runtime stops background threads without an exception
cards/8/options/2: It runs: on exit a ThreadAbortException is raised in the thread
cards/8/options/3: The process waits until the background thread finishes the file
cards/8/explain: Background threads do not hold the process. When the last foreground thread ends, they are cut off where they are, and finally does not run. For a clean exit — a cancellation token and waiting for the work.
cards/9/q: Cancel the request if the caller cancels or 10 seconds pass, and leave no subscription on someone else's token
cards/9/explain: The linked source is cancelled for either reason, CancelAfter adds the timeout, and using removes the subscription on ct when the method ends.

cards/10/pairs/0/1: A task that waits for the inner task
cards/10/pairs/1/1: A dedicated thread for blocking work
cards/10/pairs/2/1: Finish the iterations with lower indices
cards/10/pairs/3/1: A continuation without the scheduler queue
